sections.body:
A friend is a person you like, and who likes you back. At school, a friend sits near you, plays with you, and talks to you.

Friends at school begin the same way as everywhere else. One small step at a time. You say hello. You say your name. You find a thing you both like. You meet again the next day.

You do not need many friends at school. One good friend is enough for a happy day. You may have a different friend for each thing: a friend for football, a friend for books, a friend for drawing.

Some children are shy, just like you. Some children have a big group. A quiet child often notices the most. Shy is not the same as unfriendly.

Here is the good news. Making a friend is something you can practise, like tying your shoes. The more you do it, the easier it gets.

In this article you will learn how to say hello to a new child, what to talk about, how to join a game, and what to do when it feels hard.
examples: She is my friend at school.
Do you want to play with us?
sections.heading: What a friend at school is

sections.body:
A new friendship usually starts with something small. A wave. A smile. A nod.

Then you say your name. That is the whole first step. In Vietnam you might say *Chào bạn, tôi tên là Lan*. The other child tells you theirs.

Then you look for a thing you both like. Everybody has one. Football, drawing, dinosaurs, stickers, singing. You ask about it. *Bạn có thích vẽ không?*

Then you give a little time. Stay near that child for two minutes. Ask one more question. *Bạn làm gì sau giờ học?*

That is all a friendship needs to start. Not a long talk. Just a small beginning.

When you meet again the next day, say hello again. The second hello is easier than the first. After a few days, you have a friend.
examples: Hello, I am Lan. What is your name?
What do you do after school?
sections.heading: How a new friend begins

sections.body:
These are the words you need when you meet a new child. Learn them and you can use them straight away.

A **classmate** is a child in the same class as you. Classmates are the easiest people to be friends with, because you see them every day.

Introduce yourself means to say your name to somebody for the first time. That is all it means. Just your name.

Join in means to start playing with a group that is already playing. You ask first, and then you join in.

Play together means doing the same game with another child, side by side. It is the simplest friendship there is.

A **group** is two children or more. A big group is harder to join than a pair. Try to find one child first.

A **new friend** is a child you have just met. Saying hello twice makes them feel welcome.
examples: I introduced myself to the new girl.
Can I join in the football game?
sections.heading: The words for making a friend

terms.example: Mai is my classmate, and she sits next to me.
terms.gloss: A child who is in the same class as you. Classmates are the easiest people to be friends with.

terms.example: I introduced myself and said, I am An.
terms.gloss: To say your name to somebody for the first time. It only means saying your name.

terms.example: Can I join in your game?
terms.gloss: To start playing with a group that is already playing. You ask first, and then you join in.

terms.example: We play together at break time every day.
terms.gloss: To do the same game with another child, side by side. It is the simplest friendship there is.

terms.example: I have a new friend in class 4B.
terms.gloss: A child you have just met. Saying hello twice makes a new child feel welcome.

sections.body:
A group of children playing is a wall. You cannot walk through a wall. You can ask for a door.

First, walk over slowly. Running in looks loud, and loud looks scary.

Then, stand near the group and watch for a moment. Watching says *I am interested*, and it is not rude.

Next, ask one small question. *Can I play too?* That is enough. You do not need a long speech.

Then wait for the answer. A yes means you are in. A no is okay too. Say *That is fine* and go and play something else.

Finally, join in one small way at first. Stand beside somebody. Pass the ball once. Small is safe. After a minute, you will forget you were nervous.
examples: That is fine. I will play over there.
sections.heading: How to join a game that is already playing
steps: Walk over slowly to the group.
Stand near them and watch for a moment.
Join in one small way at first.

sections.body:
Talking to a new child feels hard only at the start. Good news: there are easy topics everywhere.

What are you playing? That is the best question of all. Games are easy to talk about because you are both looking at the same thing.

What did you do at home? Small children love talking about their house, their cat, their dinner.

What do you like? Ask about football, or drawing, or stickers, or a pet. Then ask a second question about the same thing.

What is in your bag? Book covers and pencils are interesting things to look at.

One thing you should not do is talk about nobody. Saying *Nobody likes him* in front of a new friend is not a good first word.

And if the other child is quiet, that is fine too. Quiet children answer in one word, and then they warm up. Be patient. A friend who is quiet often becomes the friend who stays.
examples: What did you do at home?
Do you like football or drawing?
sections.heading: What to talk about on the first day

sections.body:
Some days, making a friend does not work. That is not a sign that something is wrong with you.

A child may say no. A child may be busy. A child may be shy like you. Do not take it personally. Try again another day.

If you want to, you can try the quiet way. Give a smile. Sit near somebody. Draw next to them. Many friendships begin without a single word.

If you feel lonely most days, tell a grown-up. A teacher, a parent, someone in your family. Say it simply. *I do not have anybody to play with today.* Grown-ups can help with that.

And if somebody is unkind to you, tell an adult straight away. You will not get in trouble for telling the truth.
examples: I do not have anybody to play with today.
That is okay. I will try again tomorrow.
Can you help me find a game to join?
sections.heading: When making friends feels hard

item.summary: A friend at school is someone you meet, talk to, and play with again and again. After reading this you can say hello to a new child, join a game, find something you both like, and keep a new friendship going.
item.title: Making Friends at School
